nodes.summary: Writing $1$ for true and $0$ for false, the map sends a bit string $1^k\,0\,1^n\,0\,b$ to $1^k\,0\,1^n\,0\,\bar b$, where $\bar b$ is $b$ with every bit complemented. A bit string with fewer than two zeros goes to the fixed no-instance $1\,0\,0$.
nodes.title: Complementing map from CLIQUE to INDEPENDENT-SET instances

nodes.summary: The decision problem INDEPENDENT-SET accepts a bit string $x$ exactly when, writing $1$ for true and $0$ for false, $x = 1^k\,0\,1^n\,0\,b$ for some natural numbers $k$, $n$ and a list of bits $b$ with one entry for each pair $i < j < n$, such that the graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ given by $b$ has an independent set of exactly $k$ vertices. In that graph, distinct $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when the bit of the pair…
nodes.title: INDEPENDENT-SET

nodes.summary: Writing $1$ for true and $0$ for false, the map sends a bit string $1^k\,0\,1^n\,0\,b$ with $k \le n$ to $1^{n-k}\,0\,1^n\,0\,b$. Every other bit string, namely one of this form with $k > n$ or one with fewer than two zeros, goes to the fixed no-instance $1\,0\,0$.
nodes.title: Map from INDEPENDENT-SET to VERTEX-COVER instances

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be any property of a triple $(n, k, G)$, where $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers and $G$ is a simple graph on the vertices $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$. nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a property of a natural number $n$, a natural number $k$ and a simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. nodes.title: Fixed no-instance

nodes.summary: A literal occurrence is a triple $(c, x, b)$ of a clause index $c$, a variable index $x$ and a polarity $b$. Two occurrences $(c, x, b)$ and $(c', x', b')$ are adjacent when $c \ne c'$ and they are not complementary, that is, it is not the case that $x = x'$ and $b \ne b'$.
nodes.title: Adjacency of literal occurrences in Karp's clique graph

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ with clauses $C_0, \dots, C_{m-1}$, the list of triples $(i, x, b)$, one for each literal $(x, b)$ of each clause $C_i$, where $x$ is the variable index and $b$ the polarity. nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the list of pairs $(i, j)$ of natural numbers with $i < j < n$, in encoding order ($i$ ascending and, for each $i$, $j$ descending from $n - 1$ to $i + 1$), contains no pair twice.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the list of all pairs $(i, j)$ of natural numbers with $i < j < n$, ordered by $i$ ascending and, for each $i$, by $j$ descending from $n - 1$ to $i + 1$.
nodes.title: Vertex pairs in encoding order

nodes.summary: The map on bit strings that decodes its input as a CNF formula $\varphi$ (rejecting missing or trailing bits) and returns Karp's CLIQUE instance of $\varphi$; an input that does not decode is sent to the fixed no-instance $k = 1$ on the graph with no vertices.
nodes.title: Karp's SAT-to-CLIQUE map on bit strings

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ with $m$ clauses and $N$ literal occurrences, the bit string encoding the instance $(m, G)$: $m$ ones, a zero, $N$ ones, a zero, then one adjacency bit for each pair $(i, j)$ with $i < j < N$, listed by $i$ ascending and, for each $i$, by $j$ descending, a true bit meaning that $i$ and $j$ are adjacent. nodes.title: The graph encoded by pair bits

nodes.title: The VERTEX-COVER problem

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let the pair list of $n$ be the list of pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$ in encoding order. Let $b$ be a list of bits whose length equals the length of the pair list of $n$. For all $i < j < n$, the bit of the pair $(i, j)$ in $b$ is the entry of $b$ at the position of $(i, j)$ in the pair list of $n$.
nodes.title: Pair bits are read off by position

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a function from pairs of natural numbers to bits, and let $b$ be the list obtained by applying $f$ to each entry of the pair list of $n$ (the pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$ in encoding order). nodes.summary: For every bit string $x$, CLIQUE accepts $x$ if and only if INDEPENDENT-SET accepts the image of $x$ under the complementing map from CLIQUE to INDEPENDENT-SET instances.
nodes.title: Correctness of the complementing map from CLIQUE to INDEPENDENT-SET

nodes.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ with $m$ clauses is satisfiable if and only if Karp's graph of $\varphi$ has a clique of exactly $m$ vertices. Karp's graph has one vertex for each literal occurrence of $\varphi$, and two occurrences are adjacent when they lie in different clauses and are not complementary.
nodes.title: Karp's reduction from SAT to CLIQUE is correct

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph whose vertices are $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$, and let $k \le n$. Then $G$ has an independent set of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if $G$ has a vertex cover of exactly $n - k$ vertices.
nodes.title: Independent sets and vertex covers of complementary sizes

nodes.summary: For a mode and the Boolean saying whether a vertex $i$ is chosen, the result is true when $i$ alone settles the condition on every pair $\{i, j\}$: in the clique and independent-set modes it is true exactly when $i$ is not chosen, and in the vertex-cover mode exactly when $i$ is chosen.

nodes.summary: For every list $s$ of Booleans of length $\ell$, reading $s$ at the indices $0, 1, \dots, \ell - 1$ in turn (with default value false) gives back $s$.

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with clauses $C_0, \dots, C_{m-1}$, let $i$ and $x$ be natural numbers and let $b$ be a Boolean. The triple $(i, x, b)$ belongs to the list of literal occurrences of $\varphi$ if and only if $i < m$ and the literal $(x, b)$ belongs to $C_i$.

nodes.summary: A mode is one of three values, clique, independent set and vertex cover, naming the three graph problems CLIQUE, INDEPENDENT-SET and VERTEX-COVER that share one NP verifier.

nodes.title: The row-by-row check of the clique verifier

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and a list of bits $b$, the graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ read off $b$ has a vertex cover of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if there is a set $s$ of exactly $k$ of these vertices meeting the cover-mode pair condition on every pair $i < j$: whenever the bit of the pair $\{i, j\}$ in $b$ is set, $i$ or $j$ lies in $s$.

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $R$ a relation on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $R(i, j)$ implies $R(j, i)$. Then $R(i, j)$ holds for all $i \ne j$ if and only if $R(i, j)$ holds for all $i < j$.

nodes.summary: For literals $l = (x, p)$ and $l' = (x', q)$, each a variable $x, x' \in \mathbb{N}$ with a polarity $p, q \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, the adjacency bit of $l$ and $l'$ is false when they are complementary, that is $x = x'$ and $p \ne q$, and true otherwise. It is the adjacency of two occurrences in different clauses in Karp's graph.
nodes.title: Karp adjacency of two literals

nodes.summary: Call two literal occurrences (clause index, variable, polarity) adjacent when they lie in different clauses and are not complementary. Let $f$ be a map on occurrences such that $f(a)$ and $f(b)$ are adjacent exactly when $a$ and $b$ are, for all occurrences $a$ and $b$. Then for every list of occurrences $o_1, \dots, o_k$, the row-by-row pair bits of $f(o_1), \dots, f(o_k)$ equal those of $o_1, \dots, o_k$.

nodes.summary: For a list of literal occurrences (clause index, variable, polarity), the row-by-row pair bits are defined recursively: the empty list has none, and for a list $o, o_1, \dots, o_k$ they are the adjacency bits of $o$ with $o_k, \dots, o_1$, in that order, followed by the row-by-row pair bits of $o_1, \dots, o_k$. Two occurrences are adjacent when they lie in different clauses and are not complementary.
